To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the epididymis contains at least two cyclic AMP-dependent protein kinases, which are different in their substrate specificity, heat stability, pH activation profiles and hydroxyapatite chromatography profiles.

cyclic AMP-dependent protein kinases from rat epididymes show a high degree substrate specificity for protamines rather than histones and other proteins and are partially different from those from other tissues.
two cyclic AMP-dependent protein kinases were purified from the cytosol of rat epididymides and the kinases showed different properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the purification of cyclic nucleotide-dependent protein kinase from epididymis and the characterization of this enzyme.
the isolation of a protein kinase from rat testis and epididymis which is cyclic-AMP dependent and shows a high degree of specificity for protamine.
the purification and properties of cyclic-AMP-dependent protein kinases (PKA) from rat epididymes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cyclic AMP-dependent kinases I and II are different enzymes.
the epididymal kinases are cyclic AMP-dependent and that these kinases are distinct from other protein kinases reported in rat tissues.
the kinases from rat epididmyal cytosol are different from other cyclic AMP-dependent protein kinases reported so far.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the two kinases are different isoenzymes of cyclic AMP-dependent enzyme.
cyclic AMP-dependent protein kinases from the epididymis are different from the kinases of liver and brain.
the two kinases are distinct and are not isozymic forms of the same enzyme.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cyclic AMP-dependent protein kinases of rat epididymides are similar to the kinases of other tissues and species.
the two protein kinases are different from those reported in the literature from other tissues and that the epididymal kinases are more similar to those from testis.
cyclic AMP-dependent kinases I and II from rat epididymi are different in their substrate specificities.
